chunks: Ali, from his father, from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Abu Ayoub, from Muhammad Bin Muslim who said:

‘I heard Abu Ja’far (peace be upon him) saying: ‘I was sold (something) by a man. So when he had sold it, I arose, walked some steps, then I returned to my seat, in order for the sale to become binding when we separated’.

key_terms.لِيَجِبَ الْبَيْعُ: for the sale to become binding

ai.seo_question: How does a buyer ensure a sale is not binding until they leave the market or meeting place?
ai.summary: Imam Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) illustrates the legal mechanism of 'Khiyar al-Majlis' (option of the session) by demonstrating that the contract remains revocable as long as the parties have not fully separated from their meeting place. His specific action of walking a few steps and returning emphasizes that the 'session' is defined by the continuity of the transactional context rather than mere physical proximity, a nuance critical in Shia jurisprudence for determining when the option expires.

en.hubeali: Ali, from his father, from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Abu Ayoub, from Muhammad Bin Muslim who said,

‘I heard Abu Ja’far<sup>asws</sup> saying: ‘I<sup>asws</sup> was sold (something) by a man. So when he had sold it, I<sup>asws</sup> arose, walked some steps, then I<sup>asws</sup> returned to my<sup>asws</sup> seat, in order for the sale to become binding when we separated’.
en.sarwar: 8. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father from ibn abu ‘Umayr from abu Ayyub from Muhammad ibn Muslim who has said the following:
“I heard abu Ja‘far, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, saying, ‘I once purchased something from someone; then I got up and walked a few steps, then returned to the meeting place so that the deal becomes binding.’”
